s.t:
The Accountant position is located in a VA Medical Center within the Midsouth Healthcare Network (VISN 9). The Accountant is organizationally aligned within the Fiscal Service. Major duties include, but are not limited to: Performs daily assignments involving the review and processing of Accounting documents.

Maintains, analyzes, and reconciles general ledgers and subsidiary ledgers. Monitors and ensures compliance with Financial Indicators. Performs administrative duties such as: reviews, coordinates and monitors implementation of policies.

Assists in monitoring reports generated by FMS to identify and correct any out-of balance conditions that may exist from a variety of sources, such as: (1) the FMS interfaces with AR, CCS, FAP, IFCAP, IPPS, and transactions generated by FSC.

Uses judgement in interpreting and adapting guidelines, such as agency policies, regulations, precedents, and work directions, for application to specific cases or problems. Provides advice and assistance to technicians, analysts, and clerical personnel on transactions requiring professional accounting determinations.

Resolve operating problems by influencing or motivating individuals or groups who are working toward mutual goals. Determine proper transactions and accounts, or series of transactions to effect proper accounting entries and execute corrective action when necessary for a variety of accounting problems.

Performs internal audits, vulnerability risk assessments, and any other audits deemed necessary for the Fiscal Section as assigned. Performs numerous detailed accounting monthly reconciliations to ensure compliance with policy requirements and procedures.

Provides analysis and technical expertise for all accounting matters Studies, analyzes, and interprets manuals and other accounting regulations and policies and uses that information to complete daily tasks. Performs various assignments such as tracking on-going operations and solving problems that arise.

Reviews existing procedures and develops an appropriate method of accounting to resolve unique situations. Analyzes current procedures and systems to determine if improvement or simplification is needed.

Assists budget staff in resolving out of balance issues, developing/forecasting budget needs/excess Conducts training of both new and seasoned employees to ensure efficient and qualified coverage within the section. Uses various computer programs such as Excel, Power Point, Word, TEAMS.

Able to use time management skills effectively to determine importance of daily tasks to ensure timely completion. Works with various Service Chiefs and Administrative officers to determine spending and costing trends. Resolves out of balance issues with Treasury with research and communication.

Works with supervisor and team to provide coverage for employees that are out of office. Provides excellent customer service to include internal and external customers.

Uses effective interpersonal and communication skills in order to properly, effectively and concisely disclose the vast amount of accounting information needed by fiscal management, facility leadership, other managers throughout the facility, front line staff, vendors, veterans and VISN staff. Performs other duties as assigned.

Work Schedule: Monday through Friday; 8:00am-4:30pm Telework: This position may be authorized for telework. Ad Hoc telework only. Ad Hoc Telework. Telework that occurs on an occasional, non-routine basis.

Telework that occurs to complete short-term special assignments or to accommodate special circumstances even though the telework arrangement may occur continuously for a limited and specific period of time. Virtual: This is not a virtual position.

The education must be accredited by an accrediting body recognized by the U.S.

"Qualifications" means the combination of experience, training, education, skills, knowledge, abilities, personal characteristics, and merit factors deemed to be pertinent to successful performance.

Work may also require walking and standing in conjunction with travel to and from meetings and conferences away from the worksite.

An energetic and ambitious CA/CPA/CMA with 5+ years of experience in Accounting or Finance, who aims to build a career in Corporate Accounting. s.t:
Prepare and post journal entries related to lease additions, modifications, re-measurements, and terminations.
Assist in reviewing and interpreting lease agreements to ensure proper accounting treatment.
Maintain and reconcile lease schedules for ROU assets and lease liabilities.
Support disclosure requirements for lease accounting in financial statements.
Conduct monthly, quarterly, and annual close processes for lease accounting.

Assist in the preparation of financial statements, footnotes, and regulatory reporting related to lease assets.

Review and analyze capital project costs to ensure appropriate accounting treatment in line with US GAAP (ASC 360) and internal policies.

Collaborate with Business and FP&A teams to ensure accurate capitalization of costs and adherence to accounting policies.
Support month-end and quarter-end close processes related to fixed assets.
Prepare journal entries and account reconciliations for fixed asset activities.
Provide variance analysis and commentary for MoM, QoQ, and YoY changes.
Contribute to the preparation of materials for the CAO deck related to fixed assets.
Assist in analyzing multiple fixed asset thresholds and other related assessments.
Support the preparation of financial statements and footnote disclosures related to fixed assets.
Ensure compliance with SOX controls, company policies, and US GAAP requirements.
Monitor and ensure timely testing of internal controls, proactively addressing any deficiencies.
Support internal and external audit processes by providing required documentation and resolving audit requests promptly.
Identify and drive opportunities for process improvements and automation in fixed asset accounting.

Strong attention to detail.

## About Our Client ##
Our client is a well-established international group operating across the hospitality and leisure sector. With a growing presence in Switzerland and international markets, the organisation combines strong operational expertise with a commitment to service quality, responsible business practices and sustainable growth.
## Job Description ##
* Manage general and cost accounting activities in accordance with internal procedures, applicable regulations and reporting deadlines.
* Prepare and analyse monthly and annual financial statements in accordance with the Swiss Code of Obligations (CO) and Swiss GAAP FER.
* Contribute to the annual budgeting and forecasting process and support management with financial analysis and performance monitoring.
* Manage Swiss administrative and tax matters, including VAT, corporate taxes and social insurance requirements.
* Coordinate relationships with external auditors, banks and other financial stakeholders.
* Establish and maintain appropriate administrative procedures and key internal controls to ensure the quality and integrity of financial processes.
* Ensure the effective use of finance systems and contribute to process optimisation, automation and digitalisation initiatives.
* Support the implementation and continuous improvement of ERP and treasury solutions, such as Microsoft Dynamics 365, Kyriba or comparable systems.
* Act as a key finance contact for Swiss authorities and other external stakeholders on accounting, tax and financial matters.
* Provide local management with reliable financial information and analysis to support operational and strategic decision-making.
## The Successful Applicant ##
* Several years of professional experience in accounting and finance, ideally gained within an SME, international group or similarly complex environment.
* Strong knowledge of general and cost accounting.
* Proven experience preparing and analysing monthly and annual financial statements under Swiss GAAP FER and the Swiss Code of Obligations.
* Very good knowledge of Swiss VAT and general Swiss tax requirements.
* Experience with modern ERP and finance systems such as Microsoft Dynamics 365, SAP, Abacus, Sage or similar.
* Excellent MS Office skills, particularly Excel.
* Very good command of English; German and/or French would be an advantage.
* Autonomous, structured and analytical working style, combined with a high level of accuracy and reliability.
* Strong organisational and prioritisation skills, with the ability to manage multiple deadlines effectively.
* Solution-oriented and pragmatic personality with a strong sense of ownership.
* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to establish trusted relationships with both internal and external stakeholders.
## What's on Offer ##
* A permanent position within a stable and internationally growing organisation.
* A broad and autonomous finance role combining operational accounting with exposure to management and strategic topics.
* An environment that values collaboration, integrity, innovation and professional development.
* The opportunity to contribute to finance transformation, process optimisation and digitalisation initiatives.

By uniting applied AI research, flexible infrastructure, and seamless developer tooling, we enable companies operating at the frontier of AI to bring cutting-edge models into production.

We're growing quickly and recently raised our $1.5B Series F , led by Altimeter Capital, Conviction Partners, and Spark Capital. Join us and help build the platform engineers turn to ship AI products.

We're looking for a Revenue Accounting Manager to own billing, contract review, and revenue recognition as Baseten scales. This is a hands-on, individual-contributor role for someone who wants full ownership of the revenue cycle at a company where deal structures are getting more complex: usage-based pricing, committed capacity, credits, multi-year enterprise contracts, and new business models coming online.
You'll join Lauren, who built Baseten's quote-to-cash function from the ground up, to take on billing, contract review, and revenue recognition as deal volume and complexity grow. Having completed our first year-end audit, we're now focused on tightening contract review processes, close procedures, and reporting rigor to support the scale ahead.

You'll partner closely with Lauren, FP&A, Sales, Legal, and Revenue Operations to make sure every deal is structured, billed, and recognized correctly from day one.
Baseten is building the infrastructure layer for AI-native companies, and we're scaling quickly - in deal volume, contract complexity, and customer size. If you want real ownership over a growing function on a lean team, this role offers real scope.

Revenue Recognition and Technical Accounting
Own revenue recognition under ASC 606 across all contract types, including usage-based/consumption arrangements, committed capacity deals, credits, multi-year contracts, and new business models
Serve as the go-to person on rev rec treatment for new deal structures, products, and pricing models
Billing Operations
Own end-to-end billing: invoice generation, accuracy checks, and dispute resolution
Identify and automate manual, error-prone steps in the billing-to-cash workflow
Assist with strengthening our collections efforts and overall process
Contract Review and Deal Support
Build and maintain a standardized contract review process for Sales and Legal, flagging non-standard terms that affect recognition before deals close
Partner directly with Sales, Revenue Operations, and Legal as a proactive advisor on deal structuring
Sales and Indirect Tax
Own the sales and indirect tax process, including reviewing and maintaining our tax automation tool (nexus tracking, exemption certificates, filings), and building the governance around it as we scale into new jurisdictions
Close and Reporting
Own the revenue-related monthly close: deferred revenue rollforward, unbilled AR, credit memos, and revenue reserves
Partner with FP&A to reconcile billed vs. recognized revenue and support ARR reporting and forecasting
Own revenue-related audit deliverables, including technical memos and sample testing support

5+ years of progressive accounting experience, including 3+ years focused specifically on revenue accounting and recognition
Deep working knowledge of ASC 606, including variable consideration, multiple performance obligations, and usage-based revenue models
Hands-on experience reviewing and abstracting commercial contracts for accounting treatment
Experience owning billing operations directly, not just reviewing output from a billing team
Public company or audit-ready private company experience (Big 4 or industry, with audit exposure)
Builder mentality with a bias toward execution; comfortable operating on a lean team relative to company scale
Experience with NetSuite (or comparable ERP) and a modern billing platform
Based in San Francisco or New York, with the ability to work in-person 3+ days per week

Experience at a high-growth, venture-backed infrastructure or cloud company with usage-based or hybrid pricing
Experience with committed-use/capacity contracts
Experience overseeing sales and indirect tax compliance through an automated tax tool across multiple jurisdictions
CPA
Exposure to SOX controls in a revenue cycle context

100% coverage of medical, dental, and vision insurance for employee and dependents
Flexible PTO policy including company wide Winter Break (our offices are closed from Christmas Eve to New Year's Day!)
Paid parental leave
Fertility and family-building stipend through Carrot
Company-facilitated 401(k)
Exposure to a variety of ML startups, offering unparalleled learning and networking opportunities.
Apply now to embark on a rewarding journey in shaping the future of AI! If you are a motivated individual with a passion for machine learning and a desire to be part of a collaborative and forward-thinking team, we would love to hear from you.

You will review and analyze ERP and related accounting systems and reports for fiduciary accuracy and completeness, and initiates corrective action, as necessary.
You will review and reconcile undistributed disbursements/collections, unliquidated obligations, accounts receivable, accounts payable and performance reports.
You will prepare the Balance Sheets and Statements of Budgetary Resources.
You will attend material and financial accounting meetings and conferences, and actively participate.
In addition to the Basic Requirements for this position, your resume must also demonstrate at least one year of specialized accounting experience equivalent to the next lower grade level (GS-11) or pay band in the federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector applying principles, concepts, and practices to perform assignments concerning financial management and accounting.

Specific work experience demonstrates the following: 1) Review accounting and financial reports to identify and correct discrepancies; 2) Utilize automated financial systems to extract, interpret, and analyze financial reports and statistical data; 3) Evaluate and identify accounting system deficiencies, policy issues, and audit requirements to take or recommend corrective action; and 4) Advise and assist management on accounting and financial matters.

We are seeking a full-time Project | Staff Accountant to join our accounting team. This is a highly visible role in which you will work alongside firm leaders and project managers while reporting directly to finance and accounting leadership. Your work will directly shape decisions across the firm while you develop specialized project accounting expertise augmented by a core accounting foundation.

This role is built for a problem-solver—someone who digs into the why behind the numbers, seeks better ways of accomplishing results, and improves processes rather than just running them. You will succeed by discovering ways to optimize systems, experimenting with tools, and implementing new methods that deliver timely analysis and clearer insight.

Core responsibilities include, but are not limited to the following:

Direct the project accounting function end to end, with full accountability for making it more effective, efficient, and scalable.
Partner directly with principals, project managers, and subconsultants to deliver timely, accurate, and valuable project insight.
Drive process improvements across the Accounting Operations and Finance function that sharpen the accuracy, timeliness, and relevance of financial information.
Collaborate with the accounting team and other stakeholders to research accounting and project-related questions and implement practical, well-supported solutions.

Project accounting responsibilities include, but are not limited to the following:

Lead the project accounting function, improving its systems, workflows, and outputs to strengthen accuracy, find efficiency, and build adoption.
Collaborate with principals, project managers, and subconsultants to prepare timely and accurate client invoices consistent with contract requirements and project status.
Monitor project financial performance, including budgets, labor, expenses, revenue, remaining fees, and profitability; identify variances and risks; and communicate actionable insights to project and firm leadership.
Review contract terms, fee structures, and billing requirements to establish accurate project budgets, billing setups, invoice formats, and revenue assumptions.
Manage accounts receivable, support collection efforts, and help resolve billing questions, unbilled costs, and client payment issues.

Staff accounting responsibilities include, but are not limited to the following:

Anchor the firm's financial foundation by preparing and posting journal entries and reconciling general ledger and balance sheet accounts; you will investigate the variances you uncover and recommend corrective actions.
Equip leaders with the full financial picture by delivering recurring and ad hoc financial reports, schedules, and analyses that support management and firmwide decision-making.
Maintain complete supporting documentation for financial statements, audits, tax filings, and other compliance requirements.
Ensure the accuracy and completeness of the firm's payroll by reviewing, reconciling, and approving payroll-related activity and accounts on a recurring basis in coordination with the firm's payroll provider.
Manage tax compliance activities with external tax advisers, including preparing schedules, responding to information requests, and reviewing related filings and accounting entries.

Demonstrated record of continuous improvement, intellectual curiosity, and accountability; willing to adapt to new workflows, seek out feedback, identify opportunities for improvement, implement solutions, and take thoughtful risks that enhance efficiency and accuracy.
Strong Excel skills, including the ability to structure data to get the most out of a spreadsheet, and a track record of experimenting with tools for data analysis and reporting that improve accuracy, workflow efficiency, and understanding of the data; experience with accounting systems such as Deltek Vision or Vantagepoint is a plus.

About Agoda
At Agoda, we bridge the world through travel. Our story began in 2005, when two lifelong friends and entrepreneurs, driven by their passion for travel, launched Agoda to make it easier for everyone to explore the world.
Today, we are part of Booking Holdings [NASDAQ: BKNG], with a diverse team of over 7,000 people from 90 countries, working together in offices around the globe. Every day, we connect people to destinations and experiences, with our great deals across our millions of hotels and holiday properties, flights, and experiences worldwide.
No two days are the same at Agoda. Data and technology are at the heart of our culture, fueling our curiosity and innovation. If you’re ready to begin your best journey and help build travel for the world, join us.
The Opportunity
We are looking for an FX Controller to join our Finance team in Bangkok. This role is ideal for an experienced accounting professional with strong technical knowledge of foreign exchange, derivatives, hedge accounting and financial controls in a complex multinational environment.
You will own the accounting and controllership framework for foreign-currency transactions and exposures across multiple entities, currencies and jurisdictions. This includes FX revaluation, realized and unrealized gains and losses, derivatives, hedge-related accounting, foreign-currency intercompany transactions, exchange-rate governance and the reconciliation of Treasury systems to the general ledger.
You will be responsible for ensuring that FX accounting outcomes are complete, accurate, explainable and compliant with applicable accounting standards and internal policies. You will also provide clear analysis of material FX movements, identify unexpected exposures or accounting outcomes, and coordinate their resolution with Treasury, Controllership, Tax, Finance Systems and other Finance teams.
Beyond close and reporting ownership, you will help establish a scalable FX accounting operating model. This includes strengthening controls, improving exposure and hedge visibility, automating reconciliations and ensuring that the economic intent of Treasury activity is reflected appropriately in the financial statements.
This is a high-impact role for someone who enjoys combining technical accounting, FX and derivatives expertise, financial controllership, data analysis and cross-functional leadership.
In This Role, You'll Get To
FX Accounting and Close Ownership
Own the end-to-end accounting for foreign-currency transactions, balances, exposures and Treasury-driven FX activity across multiple entities and ledgers.
Manage monthly, quarterly and annual FX close activities, ensuring that all relevant transactions, valuations, revaluations and accounting adjustments are recorded accurately and on time.
Review and approve FX-related journal entries, including realized and unrealized gains and losses, balance-sheet revaluations, derivatives, settlements and hedge-related entries.
Ensure the correct treatment of transaction currency, functional currency, reporting currency and source-currency amounts throughout the accounting process.
Review FX results across the income statement, balance sheet and other comprehensive income, where applicable, and explain material movements to senior Finance stakeholders.
Perform reasonableness and trend analysis of FX gains and losses against exposures, market-rate movements, hedging activity, prior periods and forecasts.
Investigate unexpected FX volatility, unusual source-currency balances, duplicated or missing entries, incorrect exchange rates and other accounting exceptions.
Maintain clear visibility over outstanding FX close items, owners, financial impact and expected resolution dates.
Derivatives and Hedge Accounting
Oversee the accounting for FX derivatives, including forwards, options, swaps and other instruments used to manage foreign-currency risk.
Review derivative valuations, settlements, premiums, accruals and related general-ledger postings.
Assess and document the appropriate accounting treatment for new or non-routine FX and derivative transactions.
Support or oversee hedge designation, hedge documentation, effectiveness assessments and the ongoing accounting for qualifying hedging relationships.
Ensure accurate presentation of hedge results between the income statement, balance sheet and other comprehensive income, where applicable.
Monitor non-designated or non-qualifying hedges and ensure that their accounting impact is accurately tracked and explained.
Review hedge discontinuations, modifications, rollovers, early settlements and ineffectiveness for appropriate accounting treatment.
Support quarterly derivatives disclosures, group reporting, regulatory or survey submissions and audit requirements.
FX Exposure and Balance-Sheet Control
Develop and maintain a complete view of material foreign-currency monetary assets, liabilities, commitments and intercompany exposures.
Reconcile FX exposure information between Treasury systems, bank data, subledgers, consolidation systems and the general ledger.
Review foreign-currency cash, bank, receivable, payable, loan, cash-pool and intercompany balances for completeness and appropriate revaluation .
Oversee the accounting for foreign-currency intercompany funding, settlements, service charges and other cross-border transactions.
Ensure approved exchange rates are applied consistently, including spot rates, month-end rates, average rates, historical rates and fixed intercompany rates where required.
Challenge unexplained or unhedged exposures and work with Treasury and Finance teams to determine whether they arise from genuine economic positions, timing differences, missing transactions or accounting errors.
Establish investigation and escalation thresholds for material FX differences and unresolved reconciliation items.
Ensure significant FX-related balance-sheet accounts are reconciled, reviewed and signed off within the close timetable.
Exchange-Rate Governance and Data Quality
Own or oversee the governance of exchange rates used in ERP, Treasury, consolidation and reporting systems.
Validate that approved rates are complete, accurate , timely and consistently applied across entities and accounting processes.
Monitor interfaces between systems, market-data sources, ERP platforms and relevant tools.
Investigate differences caused by incorrect rates, stale data, currency mapping or system configurations.
Partner with Finance Systems and Treasury teams to improve the reliability and traceability of data.
Maintain appropriate evidence and approval records for rates, valuations, adjustments and system-generated entries.
Financial Reporting and Management Analysis
Deliver accurate and timely FX accounting results for management, treasury, group consolidation and statutory reporting.
Prepare clear explanations of material movements, distinguishing between operational exposure, translation effects, revaluation, hedging results, settlement timing and accounting corrections.
Partner with FP&A and Finance Business Partners to explain actual FX outcomes against forecast or budget assumptions.

## Job Description ##
Join the Finance Department as a Financial Accountant, reporting to the Accounting Team Lead, and help us maintain the highest standards of financial accuracy, compliance, and reporting excellence.
In this role, you will work in a fast-paced environment, managing a wide variety of accounting and financial reporting activities. You will use analytical skills in your day-to-day work, provide timely and accurate financial information to support decision-making, and proactively identify opportunities to improve processes and controls.
More broadly, your role will be to ensure that all business transactions and events relevant to the company's financial position are recorded accurately, comprehensively, and systematically. Together with your team, you will ensure compliance with applicable accounting principles, regulatory requirements, policies, and standards.
You will contribute to providing internal and external stakeholders with a clear and reliable view of the company's financial position and performance. As a Financial Accountant, you will also support senior management with financial planning, analysis, and reporting.

* Maintain general ledger, prepare journal entries and produce various accounting schedules/reconciliation in accordance with various GAAPSs either for the bank in Switzerland (IFRS and ARB-FINMA) or for one of the foreign subsidiaries (local GAAP).
* Prepare and review monthly, quarterly and annual financial closings. Actively participate in the half-year and year-end closing, with responsibility for specific topics and notes to the financial statements. This includes preparation of answers to external auditors.
* Investigate and resolve accounting discrepancies, unusual movements and ageing items.
* Review journal entries, accruals, provisions, prepayments and other accounting adjustments.
* Ensure appropriate accounting treatment for banking transactions and financial instruments.
* Support the preparation of statutory and management financial statements.
* Contribute to the preparation of consolidated financial reporting where applicable.
* Take responsibility in accounting projects as assigned by Management,
* Provide accounting guidance and implement appropriate solutions for complex accounting issues and queries raised by various departments and foreign group entities
* Prepare miscellaneous regulatory filings (for the SNB or FINMA as example) as assigned.

* Bachelor-s degree or equivalent diploma in accounting, finance or economics.
* Minimum 5 years- experience in a similar role ideally in the banking industry.
* You must be fluent in French and English (oral and written).
* You are adaptable and experienced in managing complex financial matters within a dynamic environment.
* You are meticulous, able to collaborate cross functionally and to work on several subjects in parallel, attentive to details with very good organisation skills.
* Strong understanding of the banking business, with the ability to see the bigger picture and understand the broader financial context.
* You have experience with IFRS and generally accepted accounting principles in Switzerland (Accounting Rules for Banks -ARB-FINMA- is a plus).
* Your skills in MS Office (Excel in particular) are excellent. Knowledge of PowerBI, SQL and/or Python are a plus.
* Knowledge of software Temenos T24 and OneStream is considered a plus.

We are looking for an experienced Senior Tax Accountant \- IFRS Tax Reporting 50% to join the Group Finance team, with a strong focus on IFRS income tax accounting. This role owns the preparation and integrity of the Group's tax notes, deferred tax positions, effective tax rate analysis, and tax provisions across our consolidated financial statements.

Prepare and review the Group's IFRS tax notes (IAS 12\) for interim and annual consolidated financial statements
Calculate, recognise, and roll forward deferred tax assets and liabilities across Group entities, including recoverability assessments

Compute and analyse the Group and entity\-level effective tax rate (ETR), identifying and explaining key drivers of movement
Perform regular cleaning and reconciliation of tax\-related balance sheet accounts (current tax payable/receivable, deferred tax assets/liabilities), resolving aged or unsupported balances
Support the quarterly and annual tax reporting cycle in close coordination with Group Consolidation and Financial Reporting
Act as a key point of contact for external auditors on tax provisions, disclosures, and technical tax accounting positions
Monitor changes in IFRS and local tax legislation relevant to Group reporting, and assess their impact on tax accounting
Provide guidance and support to local finance teams and subsidiaries on tax accounting questions and account reconciliations
Contribute to the continuous improvement and automation of tax reporting processes, templates, and account reconciliation controls
Maintain clear, audit\-ready documentation and supporting evidence for all tax positions and judgements

MCI is one of the fastest-growing tech-enabled business services companies in the USA, with a strong call center footprint and operations that extend across multiple countries.

We deliver Customer Experience (CX), Business Process Outsourcing (BPO), and Anything-as-a-Service (XaaS) cloud technology solutions across a wide range of industries, including healthcare, retail, government, education, telecom, technology e-commerce, and financial services.

Our contact centers are powered by both on-site and remote agents, leveraging advanced technologies to enhance customer journeys, drive scalability and reduce costs.
At MCI we are committed to fostering an environment where professionals can build meaningful careers, access continuous learning and development opportunities and contribute to the success of a globally expanding, industry-leading organization.
We’re seeking a proactive and detail-oriented Accountant to join our team and contribute to our continued success. This role is responsible for overseeing the company’s accounting operations, including the preparation of financial reports, maintenance of accurate financial records, and implementation of robust controls and budgeting systems. The goal is to minimize risk, ensure the integrity of financial reporting, and maintain compliance with generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP).
To be considered for this role, you must complete a full application on our company careers page, including all screening questions and a brief pre-employment test.
· POSITION RESPONSIBILITIES

Manage Accounts Receivable processes, including invoicing, applying manual payments, generating aging reports, and reconciling customer accounts.
Record routine journal entries and bank transactions accurately and timely.
Process accounts payable bills and credit card transactions as needed.
Execute month-end closing activities and perform account reconciliations.
Investigate and resolve discrepancies in financial data, ensuring accuracy and completeness.
Conduct bank reconciliations regularly.
Provide support to team members and collaborate across departments as required.

The ideal candidate for this role would share and understand the high growth objectives of Mass Markets. Demonstrated ability in an accountant role is a must. The right candidate will exhibit good business judgment and acumen and be both confident and flexible in their views.

This position will require the ability to work with multiple business units to acquire operational knowledge and execute departmental initiatives. Demonstrated interpersonal skills and oral and written communication skills are a must.
Bachelor's degree in accounting or finance
1-2 years of accrual basis accounting working experiences including accounts receivable, journal entries, month-end closing and reconciliation, and bank reconciliation.
Regular and reliable attendance is an essential function of this position
Strong oral and written communication skills; ability to interact within all levels of the organization
Demonstrates ability to successfully plan, organize and manage projects
Detail-oriented, excellent proofreading and editing skills
Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment, organized, able to prioritize and work independently
Exceptionally self-motivated and directed

MCI takes pride in tailoring our offerings to fit the needs of our diverse team across subsidiaries and locations. While specific benefits and incentives may vary by geography, the core of our commitment remains the same: rewarding effort, providing growth opportunities, and creating an environment where every employee feels valued.
If you’re ready to join a company that recognizes your contributions and supports your growth, MCI is the place for you. Apply today!

You will serve as the senior technical authority directing professional accounting operations, managing complex automated financial systems, and leading Financial Improvement and Audit Readiness (FIAR) initiatives.
You will provide expert-level management advice and independent oversight to resolve the most challenging accounting issues stemming from the commands' unique missions, isolated operating environments, and highly complex funding streams.
You will both work independently and direct team efforts to address assignments that are typically without precedent, of long duration, and require extensive cross-agency collaboration.
You will assign work to subordinate(s) based on priorities, difficulty of assignments, and the capabilities of employees.
You will directly advise the Commander and subordinate leadership on resource availability, internal controls, and the overall financial health of the command.
Your resume must also demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-13 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector.

Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: Experience managing the full range of accounting functions (e.g. financial operations, financial reporting, systems accounting, financial improvement, audit readiness) across a large and complex organization. Experience resolving complex accounting issues with a broad and significant impact.

Experience navigating financial and accounting interdependencies to resolve complex financial issues, to include: understanding organizational responsibilities and enhancing working relationships; leveraging financial systems and processes that cross organizational boundaries to resolve accounting issues and produce actionable and reliable financial information; applying change management skills to drive financial improvement; effectively advocating for financial interests of a large organization.

Experience applying quantitative analytical skills to monitor and improve financial outcomes across a large organization. Experience recommending, developing, and implementing new financial policies, processes and systems across a large and complex organization where impact to organizational mission is significant.

In addition to specialized experience, this position also has an Individual Occupational Requirement: Degree: accounting; or a degree in a related field such as business administration, finance, or public administration that included or was supplemented by 24 semester hours in accounting.

The 24 hours may include up to 6 hours of credit in business law. (The term "accounting" means "accounting and/or auditing" in this standard.

Similarly, "accountant" should be interpreted, generally, as "accountant and/or auditor.") OR, Combination of education and experience: at least 4 years of experience in accounting, or an equivalent combination of accounting experience, college-level education, and training that provided professional accounting knowledge.

The applicant's background must also include one of the following: Twenty-four semester hours in accounting or auditing courses of appropriate type and quality.

This can include up to 6 hours of business law; A certificate as Certified Public Accountant or a Certified Internal Auditor, obtained through written examination; or Completion of the requirements for a degree that included substantial course work in accounting or auditing, e.g., 15 semester hours, but that does not fully satisfy the 24-semester-hour requirement of paragraph A, provided that (a) the applicant has successfully worked at the full-performance level in accounting, auditing, or a related field, e.g., valuation engineering or financial institution examining; (b) a panel of at least two higher level professional accountants or auditors has determined that the applicant has demonstrated a good knowledge of accounting and of related and underlying fields that equals in breadth, depth, currency, and level of advancement that which is normally associated with successful completion of the 4-year course of study described in paragraph A; and (c) except for literal nonconformance to the requirement of 24 semester hours in accounting, the applicant's education, training, and experience fully meet the specified requirements.

Spreedly is the world's leading Open Payments Platform. Founded in 2007 and headquartered in Durham, NC, the company gives mid-market and enterprise businesses the infrastructure to connect to any payment gateway, processor, or fraud tool through a single API. The platform is vendor-agnostic by design, meaning customers are never locked into a single provider and never need to rebuild their payments stack to access new capabilities.
The core business problem Spreedly solves is real and costly: global merchants face a fragmented payments ecosystem, where every new market, payment method, or fraud tool typically requires a separate, time-consuming integration. Spreedly eliminates that complexity, enabling companies to route transactions intelligently, secure cardholder data, prevent fraud, and expand into new markets without heavy engineering overhead.

Spreedly is the payment orchestration platform that lets merchants, platforms, and fintechs connect to hundreds of payment services through a single integration. As we modernize our finance systems, recently moving to Rippling and rolling out Ramp later this year, we are hiring a Senior Accountant to help run a lean, highly automated accounting function.
Reporting to the Accounting Manager, this is a broad, hands-on individual contributor role on a small team. Because routine general-ledger and accounts-payable work is increasingly automated, this role is less about manual data entry and more about ownership, judgment, exception handling, and continuous improvement of how we close the books. It is a strong fit for an accountant who is comfortable across the full close, curious about new systems, and eager to put automation and AI tools to work

Record and reconcile payroll-related accounting entries (Rippling) and administer equity/stock (Carta), including related reconciliations and reporting.
Support day-to-day expense management, including reviewing, approving, and reconciling employee expense reports and corporate card transactions (e.g., in Ramp).
Take first pass on revenue recognition: enter and configure customer contracts in NetSuite under ASC 606, preparing schedules for the Controller's review and ownership.
Support the outsourced tax function by gathering schedules and requested documentation for our external provider.
Act as a power user across our finance systems (NetSuite, Rippling, Ramp), helping maintain configurations, troubleshoot, and keep integrations running cleanly.
Identify and implement process improvements: streamline close tasks, build automations, and pilot AI-enabled workflows that reduce manual effort and improve accuracy.
Support the annual audit and maintain clear process documentation for the areas you own.

Spreedly provides an open payments platform. The platform’s connectivity provides payments performance. Key products and services include:
Connect — A unified API that integrates with hundreds of payment gateways, processors, and alternative payment methods worldwide, including digital wallets. Merchants access the global payments ecosystem through one connection.
Vault — A PCI-compliant secure repository for payment methods. Merchants store card data once and reuse it across any payment service, reducing PCI scope and protecting cardholder data at scale.
Optimize — Workflow-driven routing and retry logic that directs each transaction to the best-performing gateway in real time. On average, 7.9% of failed transactions succeed immediately when retried on a secondary gateway. This is where merchants recover lost revenue and increase authorization success rates.
Protect — A flexible fraud and authentication layer, incorporating advanced fraud tools and 3DS. Following Spreedly's acquisition of Dodgeball in September 2025, fraud orchestration and payment optimization now operate within the same platform.
Resolve — Centralized management and reporting that reduces operational silos, strengthens security, and improves billing control across a merchant's entire payment operation.

As a Revenue Accounting Manager , you’ll be in charge of certain areas of the game revenue accounting at Riot Games.

This involves critical accounting player life estimates, big data transaction reconciliation and automation for micropayments, devising structure to address controls and risks including for accounts receivable, and thoughtfully developing the technical accounting for emerging revenue issues.

To be successful, you’ll need to be flexible working at both a review level and a hands-on detailed level. You will drive projects forward and collaborate with other teams including Finance, Game teams, Payments, Legal, Data, and accounting teams in our global offices.
This position reports to the Accounting Director and will play a key leadership role in the overall Accounting organization around change management, improving processes and controls, scaling accounting, company infrastructure and operations.

Deeply understand Riot’s statistical player life estimate calculation and work with a data analyst to maintain it. This includes doing analysis to explain changes, working on audit deliverables, and understanding how this estimate would apply to new products.
Reconcile large sales datasets with engineering team across the order to cash process. This data would include information from international payment processors with unique fees, FX, and taxes.
Further develop processes and automation with the engineering team to increase efficiency and scope of the large data reconciliation noted above. This includes project management, understanding system data flows, and cross team collaboration.
Research and formalize technical accounting including Principal vs Agent, Point in Time vs Over Time, Costs to obtain a contract, and Consideration payable to a customer.
Review draft contracts to ensure smooth technical accounting.
Build out approaches and systems to address key risks such as receivables collectability and chargebacks monitoring.
Project manage and oversee certain day to day, period end close, and audit related activities
Implement improved approaches to internal revenue data and systems. This may include implementing a more sophisticated revenue system and the related processes
Mentor team staff
Manage relationships with external auditors to ensure timely completion of annual audits and reviews

A bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance. Big 4 experience and a CPA designation is required.
6+ years of progressive experience with at least 3 years in a leadership role in a fast paced environment. Multinational experience is required.
Project manage key areas with multiple groups. Organize and prioritize effectively and meet deadlines while maintaining quality.
Analytical, interested in deeply understanding areas, consider why an approach is better than 1-2 alternatives.
Some statistical experience, ideally in relation to critical accounting estimates.
Strong understanding of revenue recognition in a technology/entertainment company
Comfortable working with big data processes and engineer / analysts for high volume revenue transactions.
Strong leader in training and developing high-performing individuals with a clear commitment to the development and engagement of the team. Effectively listen and demonstrate an effective, collaborative approach.

Operational experience including global high volume credit card transactions and B2B transactions.
Experience with gaming industry player life statistical estimates or similar.
Solid experience with one or more financial ERP systems, preferably Oracle

The Accounting Manager, Fixed Assets & Capital Accounting is a high-impact individual contributor role within the Corporate Accounting organization. This individual will serve as the subject matter expert and end-to-end operational owner for ŌURA’s global capital assets, corporate facility investments (including leasehold improvements and tenant allowances), internally developed software (ASC 350-40), lease accounting portfolio (ASC 842), and associated capital expenditure (CAPEX) workflows.
This role requires a seasoned accounting professional with the technical rigor to own SOX control execution, the operational initiative to design and scale agile processes as the business evolves, and the cross-functional influence to partner effectively with Engineering, Supply Chain, IT, Facilities, Marketing, and Legal.

The ideal candidate brings deep domain expertise to ensure capital assets, software investments, and lease liabilities are accurately accounted for and presented across the Balance Sheet, Income Statement, and Statement of Cash Flows, while remaining eager to support broader Corporate Accounting team initiatives.

1. Capital Asset, Real Estate, & Lease Accounting Execution
Fixed Asset & LHI Lifecycle Management: Drive end-to-end accounting for Property, Plant, and Equipment (PP&E), intangibles, Construction-in-Progress (CIP), and Leasehold Improvements (LHIs). Track facility build-outs, ensure proper capitalization timing, evaluate Tenant Improvement (TI) allowances, and align amortization schedules with lease terms.
Internally Developed Software (ASC 350-40): Own the end-to-end accounting framework for internal-use software capitalization. Establish cross-functional processes with Product, Engineering, and IT to identify qualifying projects, track stage-by-stage development costs (preliminary, application development, post-implementation), and enforce proper capitalization/amortization discipline.
Lease Accounting (ASC 842) Ownership: Manage the global corporate lease accounting portfolio, verifying contract classifications, discount rates, schedule additions/modifications, facility lease components, and monthly Right-of-Use (ROU) asset and liability reconciliations.
Cash Flow Presentation & Financial Integrity: Ensure the precise accuracy and financial statement presentation of fixed assets, capitalized software, lease liabilities, facility CAPEX, and non-cash adjustments within the primary financial statements, with a strong focus on the Statement of Cash Flows.
Impairment & Valuation Analysis: Partner with Technical Accounting to establish frameworks for evaluating asset impairment indicators (including software obsolescence, facility abandonments, or subleases), conducting annual or trigger-based valuation reviews, and executing necessary write-offs or reserve adjustments.
2. Scalable Process Design & Cross-Functional Influence
Scalable Process Architecture: Design, implement, and continuously refine agile, future-ready capital accounting processes that adapt cleanly to changes in business model, product strategy, and organizational growth.
Cross-Functional Asset Discovery: Establish proactive, cross-functional discovery procedures with IT, Engineering, Facilities, and Procurement to systematically identify capital asset purchases, new lease agreements, and software initiatives across the organization as they arise.
Policy Authoring & Operationalization: Author, update, and enforce global Capital Asset, Software Capitalization, and Lease Accounting policies, setting clear capitalization thresholds, physical inventory mandates, facility tracking rules, and documentation standards.
Business Partnership & Guidance: Serve as the primary finance contact for business partners across Facilities, Real Estate, IT, Engineering, Product, and Supply Chain, providing clear guidance on CAPEX vs. OPEX distinctions and capital project tracking.
3. Systems Evaluation, Automation, & General Corporate Accounting Support
Systems Evaluation & Transformation: Act as the business owner and lead evaluator for fixed asset management systems, lease accounting software (e.g., LeaseQuery, Lucernex, or NetSuite modules), and asset-tracking tools, partnering with IT/Transformation to automate workflows.
Ad Hoc Corporate Accounting Projects: Serve as a versatile contributor within the Corporate Accounting team, actively participating in special projects, system upgrades, technical accounting implementation, and broader close-optimization initiatives as assigned.
4. SOX Ownership, Internal Controls, & Audit
Control Ownership & Design: Own and execute SOX internal controls across Fixed Assets, Lease Accounting, and Capitalized Software domains, ensuring compliance across key control assertions: Existence, Completeness, Rights & Obligations, Valuation, and Cutoff.
Physical Inventories & Verification: Design, lead, and audit periodic physical inventory counts and fixed asset verification programs (including corporate facilities, remote office assets, and hardware) to confirm existence and condition.
Audit Interface: Serve as the primary technical point of contact for external auditors for all capital asset, LHI, capitalized software, CIP, and lease workpapers, walkthroughs, and technical memo fulfillment.

Experience: 6–8+ years of progressive corporate accounting experience, with at least 4+ years of dedicated ownership over fixed assets, capital expenditure (CAPEX), leasehold improvements, capitalized software, and lease accounting (ASC 842) in a pre-IPO or public-company environment.
Technical Mastery: Deep proficiency in US GAAP, specifically ASC 360 (Property, Plant, and Equipment), ASC 350-40 (Internal-Use Software), and ASC 842 (Leases), alongside a comprehensive understanding of capital asset impacts on the Statement of Cash Flows.
Facility & Software Expertise: Direct experience accounting for real estate transactions, facility build-outs, leasehold improvement amortization, tenant improvement (TI) allowances, and agile software development capitalization.
Individual Contributor Level: Senior Manager / Manager level expertise with the autonomy, confidence, and executive presence required to build cross-functional discovery frameworks without needing direct management authority over business partners.
SOX Expertise: Proven track record of designing, documenting, and executing SOX internal controls and leading physical asset existence and completeness audits.

Experience supporting the senior accountant with required financial reconciliations, report preparation and other financial documentation as needed.

Experience providing input for the annual financial statement audit, including assistance in responding to Prepared By Client (PBC) items, other audit requests for information, and assisting in providing information to the senior accountant to answer auditor inquiries.

Counterpart is the first Agentic Insurance™ platform, combining trusted insurance expertise with cutting-edge AI to deliver tailored management and professional liability solutions.

By integrating Agentic Underwriting™, Agentic Broker Services™, Agentic Risk Mitigation™, Agentic Claims Management™, Agentic Coverage™, and Agentic Capacity™ into one powerful platform, Counterpart empowers brokers - and the businesses they serve - to do more with less risk.

Backed by A rated carriers, Counterpart has been recognized by CB Insights as a 2025 “Top 50 Insurtech,” by Great Place to Work, and by Business Insurance as one of its 2025 “Best Places to Work.”
As Accounting Manager, you run the day-to-day financial operations within Agentic Finance - bordereau and premium reconciliation, carrier and claims payments, premium accounts receivable, accounts payable, expense management, financial reporting, audit administration, and tax filings - that keep Counterpart, Agentic Programs™, and Counterpart Insurance Company running.

You own accounts receivable, accounts payable, expense management, and vendor administration outright, and you support the Controller on bordereau, carrier payment operations, audit administration, and financial reporting - with a path to taking ownership of bordereau and carrier payment operations as those processes stabilize.

You build and run the agents that make this execution more efficient as the company scales. You report to the Controller.

Own Accounts Receivable, Accounts Payable, Expense Management, and Vendor Administration
Own premium accounts receivable from brokers end-to-end - invoicing and installment billing, cash application against policies and endorsements, and aging and collections follow-up - so premium owed to Counterpart is collected on time and applied accurately.
Own the reconciliation of broker premium remittances into the premium trust account, clearing unapplied cash before it ages and escalating past-due balances and write-off candidates to the Controller.
Own execution of Counterpart's spend-management automation - full accounts payable automation, invoice coding, and card-spend policy enforcement.
Own employee expense reimbursement administration, setting the standard for review before sign-off by Controller.
Own vendor records and documentation, including W-9 collection, and manage the relationships behind recurring vendor and brokerage-fee payments.
Own recurring program-level reimbursement invoicing end-to-end, from calculation through submission.
Support Bordereau, Carrier Payment Operations, and Claims Payments
Prepare bordereau assembly and the premium reconciliation process across all carrier and reinsurance relationships, resolving discrepancies before they reach the Controller.
Maintain the carrier payment calendar, prioritizing and resolving issues against each carrier's timing requirements for the Controller's approval.
Prepare monthly loss fund reporting to carrier partners - bank-to-book reconciliation, top-up requests, and check registers - resolving variances directly with carrier contacts.
Execute claims payments from loss fund accounts under the Controller's payment authority, partnering directly with the Claims team on payment timing and exceptions.
Support Audit Administration
Administer the response process for the annual company audit, carrier audit financial requests, and the R&D tax credit - compiling documentation, drafting responses, and managing the deadline calendar, while the Controller leads the auditor and tax-advisor relationships.
Support Counterpart Insurance Company's statutory (STAT) reporting cadence and regulatory filings, providing the underlying data and documentation the Controller needs for CIC's STAT close.
Maintain and continuously improve the accounting due dates calendar.
Support Financial Reporting
Prepare and distribute the recurring carrier partner reporting package - unaudited financials, cash position summaries, and other standard deliverables on a monthly and quarterly basis, for the Controller's review and sign-off.
Partner with the Controller on evaluating and coordinating contractor, vendor, or offshore support for these processes as the accounting function grows.
Drive Agentic Automation Across Accounting Operations
Build and use agents to automate premium receivable cash application, bordereau assembly, premium reconciliation, and claims payment processing.
Feed clean, structured financial data and workflows into Counterpart's Intelligence System.
Decide where agents replace manual work versus where judgment is still required, and partner with the technical platform team to build and continuously improve those workflows.

5-7 years of progressive accounting or finance experience, ideally at a high-growth company; insurance, insurtech, or fintech experience is a plus but not required.
A bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Working knowledge of GAAP and STAT (Statutory Accounting Principles), and comfort operating within a regulated, multi-entity insurance business.
A track record of owning and improving accounting processes end-to-end - not just executing tasks.
Hands-on experience with an accounting system or ERP (QuickBooks, NetSuite, Sage Intacct, or similar) and an AP/spend platform (Ramp, Bill.com, or similar).
A demonstrated track record of using AI tools or agents to redesign reconciliations, payment processing, and routine bookkeeping.
Comfort managing recurring payments, reconciliations, and deadline-driven filings across multiple systems and counterparties - including direct communication with banks, brokers, carriers, tax agencies, and auditors.
High attention to detail and a bias toward getting the numbers right the first time.
Clear written and verbal communication - you can represent Counterpart directly with broker, carrier, and audit contacts.
Progress toward or interest in pursuing a CPA is a plus, not required.

We're looking for a Senior Accountant / Financial Reporting specialist to join our Finance Team at Pleo. In this role, you'll help strengthen core accounting execution, audit management, and monthly consolidated results analysis while being part of a high-growth environment as we scale our financial infrastructure. If you're excited about leveraging AI and automation to redefine modern accounting with a strong focus on IFRS excellence and financial rigor, then this is the opportunity for you!
Who you’ll be working with and reporting to
You’ll report to our Accounting Associate Director and work closely with teams across the Finance organisation. You will be part of a team dedicated to technical rigor and operational efficiency, partnering with cross-functional departments to elevate our accounting processes to the next level.
What you’ll be doing

s.h: As a Senior Accountant, you will
s.t:
Prepare and post journal entries, perform balance sheet reconciliations, and drive high standards for period close improving quality and speed.
Own the preparation of audit schedules, coordinate responses to requests, and drive the closure of audit questions to ensure a predictable, well-documented process.
Deep dive into monthly results, flagging risks, unusual transactions, and key movements while providing decision-ready insights for finance leadership.
Identify accounting risks, implement practical mitigations, and strengthen internal controls to ensure our processes are scalable and accurate.
Actively leverage AI tools to improve efficiency and consistency, identifying opportunities to standardise and simplify recurring accounting work.

s.h: You’ll thrive in this role if you have
s.t:
6+ years of experience with a strong ability to apply IFRS in real-world scenarios.
Comfort working with consolidated results, analysing variances, and exercising complex accounting estimates and judgments.
Proven experience managing audits end-to-end or acting as the primary finance contact for external auditors.
A track record (or clear potential) of using AI and automation to improve accounting outcomes and efficiency.
The ability to operate effectively in a fast-changing environment with an "ownership mindset" and excellent judgment.
Strong ability to translate complex accounting issues into scalable process improvements and clear insights for stakeholders.
Why is this role a good fit for you

s.h: This role is a good fit for you if
s.t:
You want genuine agency at group level rather than executing instructions handed down by a central team
You'd rather design a process than inherit one, and you want to see your own work implemented
You like variety. This is a different topic most days, not a fixed monthly cycle

s.h: This role is not a good fit for you if
s.t:
You want a settled, mature environment where the process is set and the day looks the same. That's the clearest reason this role doesn't work out for people
You need stable priorities. It's volatile here. Several topics run at once, progress depends on other people, and priorities can change overnight
You want to stay inside accounting. A large part of the job is working with teams outside Finance and with external advisors in each country
How you’ll develop in this role

s.h: In your first 6 - 12 months at Pleo, you’ll
s.t:
Lead the Audit Readiness initiative to drive impact in our year-end execution and documentation standards.
Collaborate with the Finance team to embed AI-forward ways of working, automating manual workflows to increase team capacity.
Grow your skills in process improvements and financial analysis, taking on new challenges as the company continues to scale across our legal entity markets.
We’re committed to helping you develop your career, whether that means taking on bigger leadership projects, mastering the intersection of AI and Finance, or deepening your expertise in complex consolidated reporting.

We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows:
Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background.
Hiring manager interview: A conversation with our Accounting Associate Director covering your technical accounting and IFRS experience.
Team panel and Pleo challenge: You'll meet the hiring manager, his manager and a peer from the team. The challenge is presented live in the session, so there's nothing to prepare or send in advance. We're looking at how you handle complexity, new areas and stakeholders.
Final interview: A closing conversation, used where it's helpful for both sides.
Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success!
Last time we hired this role, we received a lot of applications but can only interview a finite number of people. Some of the key reasons why previous candidates didn’t make it past the application screening stage include:
CV writing and content: we receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI—it’s a big focus for us internally too—but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light.

What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on.

A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background!
